hi there, thanks for your PR.
It seems the device manager recovery needs some more attention. I'm investigating a similar bug which will require changes in this flow, pretty similar to the ones made here.
I'll review this PR shortly. Meanwhile, could you please squash the two commits, because it seems the second is only a tiny cleanup of the first, and fix the automated checks (e.g. https://prow.k8s.io/view/gs/kubernetes-jenkins/pr-logs/pull/102717/pull-kubernetes-typecheck/1404497949060239360 ) ?
Thanks!

Just like we are not being able to retrieve topology info from checkpoint file, device health is another data point which will get incorporated as part of the checkpoint with your change. Based on the current behavior of device plugin and how checkpoint file is updated, it appears to me that the checkpoint file is updated either when pods requesting devices are created (when Allocate is called and not at the time of deallocation of devices) or when device plugins are deleted from a cluster removing the registered devices corresponding to those device plugins from the checkpoint. But the the main concern I would have is that given that checkpoint file at a given time might not reflect the exact current state of devices running on the pod, how do we make sure that the device health (which can change unlike topology) is correctly represented in the checkpoint file? It would be interesting to see how device health info is handled currently by device manager when kubelet restarts given that it does not expose this information in the checkpoint file?

issue_context.title: when the node restarts, the numa information of the device cannot be obtained from the checkpoint
issue_context.body:
<!-- Please use this template while reporting a bug and provide as much info as possible. Not doing so may result in your bug not being addressed in a timely manner. Thanks!

If the matter is security related, please disclose it privately via https://kubernetes.io/security/
-->


#### What happened:
When the node restarts, the numa information of the device cannot be obtained from the checkpoint(maybe device plugin start slow), resulting in an error in the cpuset setting.

Through the tracking code, it is found that when the kubelet is restarted, the Topology information is not retained in the checkpoint.
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/ea0764452222146c47ec826977f49d7001b0ea8c/pkg/kubelet/cm/devicemanager/topology_hints.go#L131-L139

`m.allDevices` is nil.



#### What you expected to happen:
`m.allDevices` can restore from checkpoint.Can get the numa information correctly 

#### How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible):
- The device plugin reports the device information and the associated numa, and normally schedules a pod to the node
- Restart node, the device plugin may not be started yet, or it may be slow to start. At this time, the original container is being started gradually
- kubelet print message "[topologymanager] Hint Provider has no preference for NUMA affinity with any resource"
- the origin container can not get numa from device plugin

#### Anything else we need to know?:

#### Environment:
- Kubernetes version (use `kubectl version`):
- Cloud provider or hardware configuration:
- OS (e.g: `cat /etc/os-release`):
- Kernel (e.g. `uname -a`):
- Install tools:
- Network plugin and version (if this is a network-related bug):
- Others:
comments:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/e52b7be7d719673a1a5ae28ad3bb0d6db58d35ec/pkg/kubelet/cm/devicemanager/endpoint.go#L96-L121

It seems that Device is not ready, I think it is unnecessary to store AllDevices.


Maybe adjust the startup sequence of Device and Kubelet, it might be better to move Device to the front of Kubelet.
But the startup sequence is uncontrollable, or when the abnormal situation of node restart occurs, or the device itself starts slowly?
If the Device is not actually ready, and the Kubelet assumes it is ready, will it introduce new bug?

This will only affect pods that have been scheduled to node. If the device is not ready(In other words, even if it is ready, all device information is not reported), then kubelet cannot obtain device related information, and the information obtained by kubelet from checkpoint does not record numa related information. Resulting in failure to obtain topology information, and ultimately affect the setting of cpuset.

> If the device is not ready(In other words, even if it is ready, all device information is not reported)

The above statement is not clear to me.
I tried reproducing this issue but noticed that after kubelet restart the topology information of the device allocated to the running pod is getting repopulated in the checkpoint file. Can you please add more description on the how to exactly reproduce this issue? Are we saying that this issue occurs when the device plugin is not ready and kubelet restart occurs? I would like to gain a better understanding of exactly the circumstances under which we encounter this bug.

Meet several conditions:
1. The kubelet restarts
2. The device plugin has not reported device information in time
3. Only containers that have been running on the original node (without rescheduling) will get the error numa information

In the restart flow, the kubelet should reset the allocatable device count to zero until the device plugin register itself again (https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/release-1.21/pkg/kubelet/cm/devicemanager/manager.go#L517).
Which can be slow indeed, but pods should not reach the node until devices are reported allocatable.
When the device plugin registers itself again, it will report topology information, so we're good.

It seems to me that you possibly just hit https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/102880 maybe?
@silenceper  would you confirm if it is dupped to #102880?
I looked at the issue  #102880, and from my point of view, it does not seem to be the problem I encountered here.

thanks for updating the reproduction steps.
Unfortunately is still not very clear how to reproduce the issue. The steps you added document what happens when the condition triggers. What we miss is the steps to reproduce the state which makes it possible for the condition to trigger, so we can properly assess the bug severity.
For example:
- do we need a special device plugin or does it happen with any device plugin?
- do we need a particulat combination of pods or just one pod requesting devices is enough?
- do the pod need to be static or any combination of pods is sufficient?
- does the issue happen with a simple kubelet restart or do after a node drain?
- what triggered the kubelet restart? perhaps a crash? was the restart triggered by a kubelet update?

Ideally, the reproduction steps should allow us to write a end to end (e2e) test which reproduces the bug and validates the fix, preventing regressions: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/102882/commits/ca593e562f7913ef14eff0647d3c97da125c3cf7

Yep, I am curious too here as well why this was moved from pkg/kubelet/cm/devicemanager/pod_devices.go to a new package `device`? In addition to not being able to understand the motivation behind this change, it breaks some of this unit tests in manager_test.go and topology_hints_test.go as the you would have to import the correct package where the types are defined.
If you do not reuse a new package,cause an error "import cycle not allowed"
This is also to ensure that after the kubelet is upgraded, the check verify sum can be successful, and it will be treated as an object of the old version here.
Why change to V2 instead of adding directly to the original?
Mainly to ensure that the check verify sum can be successful after the kubelet is upgraded.
Why do we need both `RegisteredDevices` and `AllDevices` as both have information corresponding to devices that are registered to Kubelet?
